mainTopic: Yoma 80b: The eating and drinking measures on יום הכפורים, what foods combine toward the ככותבת, and why אכילה גסה does not count as eating
overview: This amud opens by finishing an earlier point: in the case of עוג מלך הבשן, בית שמאי turn out to hold the stricter view about the drinking measure. Then רבי זירא challenges אביי three times about the measures on יום הכפורים. He asks why eating has one fixed measure (ככותבת) while drinking depends on each person's own cheekful, whether a giant like עוג can be satisfied by a date's worth, and whether fatty meat and grapevine shoots satisfy equally. אביי answers each time that חז"ל have a tradition that a ככותבת always settles the mind (מיתבא דעתיה) at least somewhat. רבא then questions the time limit of כדי אכילת פרס, and רב פפא explains that טומאת גוויה is only rabbinic, with its פסוק serving as an אסמכתא. Next, on the משנה's words 'כל האוכלין', the גמרא teaches that salt joins meat, and brine joins a vegetable, because anything that prepares food counts as food. Finally, ריש לקיש teaches that overfull eating (אכילה גסה) is not real eating: on יום הכפורים the person is פטור, and a זר who overeats תרומה pays the קרן but not the חומש. רבי ירמיה then begins a parallel teaching from רבי יוחנן that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The question was asked about עוג, so בית שמאי end up stricter
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes an earlier discussion. The question about the drinking measure was asked about עוג מלך הבשן, whose cheekful is huge, so in his case בית שמאי's measure (רביעית) is the stricter one.
steps.simpleTranslation: When this question was asked, it was asked about עוג מלך הבשן, for whom בית שמאי turn out to be the strict ones.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing an answer to a question on the previous amud. It explains that the case being discussed was a giant like עוג, not a regular person.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For a normal person, a cheekful (מלא לוגמיו) is less than a רביעית, so the cheekful measure is the stricter one. For עוג, a cheekful is far more than a רביעית. So for him, בית שמאי's רביעית is the smaller amount, and a smaller measure means stricter liability.

keyTerms.meaning: It was asked
Og, king of Bashan, a famous giant
The school of Shammai
On the strict side

steps.confusionAlert: A smaller measure is STRICTER, because you become liable sooner. So whoever gives the smaller amount is the 'strict' opinion.

phrases.english: When it was asked,
it was asked about Og, king of Bashan,
where Beit Shammai turn out to be stringent.
phrases.notes: עוג's cheekful is much bigger than a רביעית.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי אִתְּשִׁיל, בְּעוֹג מֶלֶךְ הַבָּשָׁן אִתְּשִׁיל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers a question raised at the end of the previous amud (80a) about whether this is one of בית שמאי's leniencies.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case (giant rather than normal person)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: For a normal person, בית שמאי's רביעית is the more lenient measure.
steps.terutzMaskana: The question was about עוג, for whom רביעית is the stricter measure.

steps.title: Why is eating fixed but drinking personal?
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא asks why eating has one fixed measure for everyone (ככותבת), while drinking depends on each person's own cheekful.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא objected: Why is eating different, where everyone has the same measure of a large date? And why is drinking different, where each person goes by his own measure?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא attacks an apparent inconsistency between the eating measure and the drinking measure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both measures exist to show when a person's suffering on יום הכפורים has been broken. So it seems they should work the same way. Either both should be fixed or both should depend on the person.

keyTerms.meaning: He objected strongly to it
רבי זירא, the questioner
What is the difference?
The size of a large date, the eating measure
By his own (measure)

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira strongly objects to this:
What is different about eating,
that each and every person goes by a large date's volume,
and what is different about drinking,
that each and every person goes by his own measure?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַבִּי זֵירָא: מַאי שְׁנָא אֲכִילָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the בית שמאי/בית הלל point to a new challenge about the measures themselves.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that eating is fixed (ככותבת) while drinking is personal (מלא לוגמיו).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: There is no obvious reason for the two measures to work in different ways.

steps.title: A date settles anyone, but only your own cheekful settles you
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that חז"ל have a tradition: a date's worth of food settles anyone's mind. With drinking, only a person's own cheekful settles him.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: The Rabbis know that with a large date's worth a person's mind is settled, and with less it is not. With drinking, his own cheekful settles his mind, but his friend's smaller cheekful does not.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי explains that each measure is based on what actually relieves a person's suffering.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The shared goal is the point where a person feels relieved (מיתבא דעתיה). For food, there is a known fixed amount that does this for everyone. For drink, the feeling depends on how much fits in your own mouth.

keyTerms.meaning: אביי, the one who answers
The Rabbis have it as an established tradition
His mind is settled, i.e., he feels relieved
Less than this
With his friend's (measure)

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the key idea for the whole sugya. Every measure on יום הכפורים is about יתוב הדעת, the point where the suffering is relieved.

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
The Rabbis have a tradition regarding a large date's volume,
that with this amount his mind is settled,
less than this, it is not settled.
With drinking, with his own amount his mind is settled,
with his friend's amount, his mind is not settled.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי: קִים לְהוּ לְרַבָּנַן בִּכְכוֹתֶבֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי זירא's first challenge.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing based on received tradition and reality
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Eating and drinking should follow the same pattern.
steps.terutzMaskana: Each measure follows what actually relieves the person. A date does this for anyone, but a cheekful only works if it is your own.

steps.title: Can a giant like עוג be satisfied with a date?
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא asks whether one date's worth of food could really satisfy both a normal person and a giant like עוג.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא objected: Is all the world satisfied with a large date, and עוג מלך הבשן also with a large date?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא challenges אביי's claim that a date settles everyone, using the extreme example of a giant.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the measure is based on feeling relieved, a giant should need far more food. That would mean eating should also be a personal measure, just like drinking.

keyTerms.meaning: The whole world, i.e., everyone of normal size
Halachic measure, the minimum amount for liability
Affliction, the suffering required on יום הכפורים

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira strongly objects to this:
Is the whole world satisfied with a large date,
and Og, king of Bashan, also with a large date?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַבִּי זֵירָא: וְכׇל הָעוֹלָם כּוּלּוֹ בִּכְכוֹתֶבֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks אביי's answer in Step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's claim that ככותבת settles everyone's mind.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Body size should change how much food relieves hunger, so one fixed measure seems unreasonable.

steps.title: Everyone is settled, just by different amounts
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that a date settles everyone's mind at least a little. A normal person is settled a lot, and עוג only a little, but both count.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: The Rabbis know that with this amount the mind is settled and with less it is not. However, regular people are settled a lot, and עוג מלך הבשן only a little.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי refines his answer. The fixed measure does not claim that everyone feels equally full.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The test is not whether a person is fully satisfied. The test is whether he has some relief at all. Even for עוג, a date gives a little relief, and that is enough to count as eating.

keyTerms.meaning: However
Everyone, i.e., normal people
A lot, greatly
A little

steps.confusionAlert: אביי is NOT saying עוג is fully satisfied by a date. He is saying the date gives some relief, and some relief is all that is needed.

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
The Rabbis have a tradition
that with this amount his mind is settled,
less than this, his mind is not settled;
however, everyone else is settled a lot,
and Og, king of Bashan, only a little.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי: קִים לְהוּ לְרַבָּנַן דִּבְהָכִי מִיַּתְּבָא דַּעְתֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי זירא's second challenge.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Clarifying the standard (some relief, not full relief)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A fixed measure would require everyone to feel equally satisfied.
steps.terutzMaskana: A date gives some relief to everyone, even if the amount of relief differs.

steps.title: Does fatty meat satisfy like grapevine shoots?
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא asks whether a date's worth of rich fatty meat and a date's worth of thin grapevine shoots could really satisfy the same way.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא objected: Fatty meat at a large date's volume, and grapevine shoots also at a large date's volume?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא challenges the fixed measure again. This time the question is about the type of food, not the size of the person.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Rich food fills you much more than light food. If the measure is about relief, the type of food should change the measure.

keyTerms.meaning: Fatty meat, a very filling food
Young grapevine shoots, a light and barely filling food
Liability for כרת, the punishment for eating on יום הכפורים

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira strongly objects to this:
Fatty meat at a large date's volume,
and grapevine shoots also at a large date's volume?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַבִּי זֵירָא בָּשָׂר שָׁמֵן בִּכְכוֹתֶבֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third attack, now based on the type of food.
steps.kashyaTarget: The single ככותבת measure for all foods.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Different foods satisfy very differently, so one fixed measure seems unreasonable.

steps.title: Every food settles the mind, just to different degrees
steps.stepSummary: אביי gives the same answer as before. A date's worth of any food gives some relief: fatty meat a lot, grapevine shoots only a little.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: The Rabbis know that with this amount the mind is settled and with less it is not. However, fatty meat settles a lot, and grapevine shoots only a little.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי closes the discussion using the same principle he used for עוג.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The fixed measure promises some relief, not equal relief. So differences in food type, like differences in body size, do not change the measure.

keyTerms.meaning: That with this (amount)
Settling of the mind, the basis for the measures
Fixed measure

steps.whatToRemember: The eating measure on יום הכפורים is ככותבת for everyone and every food. חז"ל have a tradition that this amount always gives some relief (יתוב הדעת), even if the relief is small. Drinking is different: only a person's own cheekful relieves him.

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
The Rabbis have a tradition
that with this amount his mind is settled,
less than this, his mind is not settled.
However, fatty meat settles it a lot,
and grapevine shoots only a little.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי: קִים לְהוּ לְרַבָּנַן דִּבְהָכִי מִיַּתְּבָא דַּעְתֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי זירא's third challenge with the same principle used in Step 5.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Applying the 'degree of relief' principle to food type
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Weak foods should need a bigger measure.
steps.terutzMaskana: Every food at ככותבת gives some relief, so the measure stays fixed.

steps.title: רבא questions why a big date gets the same time limit as an olive
steps.stepSummary: רבא asks why a כותבת, which is bigger than a כזית, must be eaten within the same time limit of כדי אכילת פרס.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא objected: For all forbidden foods, a כזית counts if eaten within the time it takes to eat a פרס. And on יום הכפורים, a כותבת also counts only if eaten within that same time?!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא raises a challenge. A כותבת is bigger than a כזית, yet the גמרא gives both the same time window of כדי אכילת פרס.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a person must eat a כזית within the time of eating a פרס for the eating to count as one act. On יום הכפורים the amount is bigger, a כותבת, but the time window stays the same. רבא asks: if the amount is bigger, shouldn't the person get more time to eat it?

keyTerms.meaning: He strongly objected to it; a forceful challenge
An olive's volume; the standard minimum for forbidden eating
A large date's volume; the minimum for eating on יום הכפורים
The time it takes to eat a half-loaf; the window within which eating combines into one act

phrases.english: Rava strongly objected to it:
An olive-bulk within the time of eating a half-loaf,
phrases.notes: The general rule for all forbidden foods

phrases.english: and a large date-bulk also within the time of eating a half-loaf?!
phrases.notes: The amount is bigger, but the time is the same

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רָבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the size of the כותבת has been defended, רבא now attacks the time window used for it.
steps.kashyaTarget: Using the same time window of כדי אכילת פרס for a כותבת as for a כזית
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A bigger amount should logically be given a longer time to eat, so the identical window seems inconsistent.

steps.title: אביי: eating within this time is what settles the mind
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that חז"ל have a tradition: eating within this time settles the mind, and eating over a longer time does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: The רבנן know by tradition that eating within this time settles a person's mind. Eating over a longer time does not settle his mind.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי defends the time window. On יום הכפורים, what matters is whether the eating ends the person's suffering, and that only happens when he eats within this time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The יום הכפורים measure is not about the size of the food alone. It is about ending the person's state of affliction. If he eats a כותבת slowly over a longer time, he never feels relieved, so it does not count as breaking his עינוי.

keyTerms.meaning: The רבנן have it as an established tradition
His mind is settled; he feels relieved
More; longer

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
The Sages have an established tradition
that within this amount of time his mind is settled;
within more time than this,
his mind is not settled.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי: קִים לְהוּ לְרַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבא's challenge from step 8.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Received tradition about the purpose of the measure (settling the mind)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A bigger amount should get a longer eating window.
steps.terutzMaskana: Relief from affliction only comes when eating within כדי אכילת פרס, so the window stays fixed.

steps.title: רבא compares it to the half-loaf measure for impurity
steps.stepSummary: רבא challenges again: the measure for becoming impure through eating is half a פרס, yet it must also be eaten within the time of eating a פרס.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא objected: A כותבת must be eaten within the time of eating a פרס, and half a פרס must also be eaten within the time of eating a פרס?!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא brings a second challenge from a different area of law: becoming impure by eating impure food.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For impure food to make the eater's body impure, he must eat half a פרס, a much larger amount than a כותבת. Yet both amounts are given the same time window of כדי אכילת פרס. רבא asks how one time limit can fit two such different amounts. If the window is set by when the mind is settled, why should it not change with the amount?

keyTerms.meaning: Half of a half-loaf; the measure for becoming impure by eating impure food

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the words. פרס itself already means a half-loaf, so 'חצי פרס' is half of that (about two eggs' volume). The 'time of eating a פרס' is a time measure, and 'חצי פרס' is an amount of food.

phrases.english: Rava strongly objected to it:
A large date-bulk within the time of eating a half-loaf,
phrases.notes: The word in parentheses is a textual variant in the printed text

phrases.english: but half a half-loaf within the time of eating a half-loaf?!
phrases.notes: Refers to the measure for impurity contracted through eating impure foods

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רָבָא: (בְּכוֹתֶבֶת) בִּכְדֵי אֲכִילַת פְּרָס
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the window is defended for a כותבת, רבא tests it against a much larger measure.
steps.kashyaTarget: Applying the כדי אכילת פרס window to the large measure of חצי פרס for impurity
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A כותבת and a much larger חצי פרס are given the identical כדי אכילת פרס window, so the window does not seem tied to the amount eaten.

steps.title: רב פפא: leave aside body impurity, since it is only rabbinic
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא answers that no proof can be brought from טומאת גוויה, because it is not a Torah law.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said to him: Leave aside טומאת גוויה, because it is not from the Torah.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא pushes away רבא's comparison. The law about becoming impure by eating impure food is rabbinic, so its rules cannot be used to challenge Torah measures.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since חז"ל created this impurity, they could set its measures however they chose, including a lenient time limit. A rabbinic law with its own rules does not challenge the logic of the יום הכפורים measure.

keyTerms.meaning: Leave it aside; don't bring a proof from it
Impurity of the body that comes from eating impure food
From the Torah; Torah law

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said to him:
Leave aside ritual impurity of the body,
since it is not by Torah law.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב פָּפָּא: הַנַּח לְטוּמְאַת גְּוִויָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבא's challenge in step 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing a rabbinic law from a Torah law
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Every measure that uses the כדי אכילת פרס window should follow the same logic.
steps.terutzMaskana: טומאת גוויה is rabbinic and has its own rules, so it proves nothing about Torah measures.

steps.title: Didn't רב פפא himself say body impurity is from the Torah?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that רב פפא elsewhere learned from a פסוק that טומאת גוויה is from the Torah.
steps.simpleTranslation: Did רב פפא really say this? But it is written: 'Do not make yourselves impure with them, that you become impure through them.' And רב פפא said: From here we learn that טומאת גוויה is from the Torah!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב פפא with his own words. He seems to contradict himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 11 רב פפא called טומאת גוויה rabbinic. Yet he also used a פסוק in ויקרא to show it is a Torah law. The גמרא asks which of his statements he really holds.

keyTerms.meaning: Did he really say so? (introduces a contradiction)
But isn't it written?
From here; this is the source

phrases.english: But did Rav Pappa really say this?
But isn't it written:
"Neither shall you make yourselves impure with them, that you should be impure thereby"
And Rav Pappa said:
From here we learn that ritual impurity of the body is by Torah law!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא הָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer given in step 11 by quoting רב פפא against himself.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב פפא's claim that טומאת גוויה is not from the Torah
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב פפא himself derived טומאת גוויה from a פסוק, which seems to make it a Torah law.

steps.title: It is rabbinic, and the verse is only a hint
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that טומאת גוויה is rabbinic, and the פסוק רב פפא quoted is only an אסמכתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is from the רבנן, and the פסוק is just an אסמכתא, a supporting hint.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the contradiction. רב פפא always held the law is rabbinic. He only quoted the פסוק as a hint that the רבנן attached to their law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An אסמכתא is a פסוק that חז"ל attach to a rabbinic law as a hint, not as its real source. So both of רב פפא's statements fit together: the law is rabbinic, and the פסוק just decorates it. This keeps the answer from step 11 standing.

keyTerms.meaning: From rabbinic law
Merely a supporting hint from a verse, not the true source

steps.whatToRemember: טומאת גוויה (becoming impure by eating impure food) is rabbinic. A פסוק quoted for it is only an אסמכתא, so its measures cannot challenge Torah measures like the כותבת of יום הכפורים.
steps.confusionAlert: When the גמרא quotes a פסוק, it does not always mean the law is from the Torah. An אסמכתא looks like a Torah source but is only a hint for a rabbinic law.

phrases.english: It is by rabbinic law,
and the verse is a mere support.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִדְּרַבָּנַן, וּקְרָא אַסְמַכְתָּא בְּעָלְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 12.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the verse as an אסמכתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב פפא's use of a פסוק means he held טומאת גוויה is from the Torah.
steps.terutzMaskana: The law is rabbinic, and the פסוק is only a supporting hint.

steps.title: Meat and its salt combine for the measure
steps.stepSummary: On the משנה's words 'כל האוכלין', רב פפא teaches that meat eaten with salt combines toward the כותבת, because people eat them together.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'All foods' combine. רב פפא said: If someone ate meat and salt, they combine. Even though salt alone is not 'eating', since people eat them together, they combine.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the משנה and starts a new topic: which items join together to reach the כותבת measure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Salt by itself is not considered food, so eating salt alone would not count. But meat is normally eaten with salt, so the salt becomes part of the meal and counts toward the כותבת. The test is how people normally eat.

keyTerms.meaning: Raw or roasted meat
Salt
Combines; joins together toward the minimum measure
Since people commonly eat it this way

phrases.english: We learned in the mishna: "All foods" combine.
phrases.notes: Quote from the משנה, opening a new discussion

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
If one ate meat and salt, they combine.

phrases.aramaic: וְאַף עַל גַּב דְּלָאו אֲכִילָה הִיא,
phrases.english: And although eating salt is not considered eating,
since people eat it this way,
they combine.

steps.triggerLanguage: כׇּל הָאוֹכָלִין. אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new section that comments on a phrase in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Meat and the salt eaten with it combine toward the כותבת, because people normally eat them together.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that what counts as 'eating' on יום הכפורים depends on normal eating habits, not on each item alone.

steps.title: ריש לקיש: brine on a vegetable combines
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש teaches that the brine on a vegetable combines with the vegetable toward the כותבת on יום הכפורים.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said: The brine on top of a vegetable combines toward the כותבת on יום הכפורים.
steps.whatsHappening: A second teaching in the same direction: the liquid on a pickled or salted vegetable counts together with the vegetable.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Brine is wet like a drink, but it comes on the vegetable as part of the food. ריש לקיש rules that it joins the vegetable to make up the כותבת. The גמרא will next ask why this needed to be said.

keyTerms.meaning: Brine; salty liquid from pickling
A vegetable

phrases.english: Reish Lakish said:
Brine that is on a vegetable
combines toward the large date-bulk on Yom Kippur.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ: צִיר שֶׁעַל גַּבֵּי יָרָק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a parallel case to רב פפא's teaching about meat and salt.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Brine on a vegetable combines with the vegetable toward the כותבת on יום הכפורים.

steps.title: Isn't that obvious?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why ריש לקיש needed to teach this, since it seems obvious.
steps.simpleTranslation: That is obvious!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges ריש לקיש's statement as unnecessary. This sets up the next step, which explains what new point he is teaching.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Brine sits on the food and is eaten with it, so it seems clear that it should count. The גמרא assumes every teaching must add something, so it asks what the חידוש is here.

keyTerms.meaning: It is obvious! (Why say it?)

phrases.english: It is obvious!

steps.triggerLanguage: פְּשִׁיטָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions whether step 15 teaches anything new.
steps.kashyaTarget: The need for ריש לקיש's statement
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the ruling is self-evident, there is no reason for an אמורא to state it.

steps.title: Whatever prepares food counts as food
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that one might have thought brine is a drink, which does not join with food. The teaching shows that anything that prepares food is itself food.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said brine is a drink. So ריש לקיש teaches us: anything that makes food ready to eat is itself counted as food.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the חידוש of ריש לקיש and gives a broad principle.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Food and drink are measured separately on יום הכפורים and do not combine. Since brine is liquid, one might think it is a drink and does not join with the vegetable. The rule כל אכשורי אוכלא אוכלא הוא says that because brine serves to prepare the food, it is treated as food.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have said (introduces a mistaken assumption)
A drink; a liquid
It teaches us (the new point)
Things that prepare or improve food

steps.whatToRemember: On יום הכפורים, items eaten as part of food join the כותבת measure. Salt joins meat because people eat them together, and brine joins a vegetable because כל אכשורי אוכלא אוכלא הוא: anything that prepares food is food.

phrases.english: Lest you say it is a beverage,
he teaches us:
anything that prepares food is itself food.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַהוּ דְּתֵימָא מַשְׁקֶה הוּא, קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the פשיטא challenge of step 16.
steps.terutzResolutionType: מהו דתימא / קא משמע לן: identifying the חידוש
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Brine is a liquid, so it should count as a drink and not join with the food.
steps.terutzMaskana: Anything that prepares food counts as food, so the brine joins the vegetable toward the כותבת.

steps.title: Overfull eating on יום הכפורים is exempt
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש rules that one who eats אכילה גסה on יום הכפורים is פטור, because the Torah speaks of 'affliction', and this excludes someone who is only harming himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said: Someone who eats in an overfull way on יום הכפורים is exempt. Why? The verse says 'who will not be afflicted', and that excludes someone who is harming himself.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new teaching from ריש לקיש: if someone is already stuffed and forces down more food on יום הכפורים, he is not punished. ריש לקיש also gives the reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah never says 'do not eat' on יום הכפורים. It says a person must be 'afflicted' (תעונה). A person who eats when already overfull is not removing his affliction. He is actually hurting himself, so he has not broken the מצוה of עינוי.

keyTerms.meaning: Overfull eating: eating when already stuffed, so the food gives no benefit
Exempt from punishment
What is the reason?
Will be afflicted: the Torah's word for the יום הכפורים fast
Excluding one who harms himself

steps.confusionAlert: פטור here means no punishment. It does not mean the person was allowed to eat in the first place. The case is someone already completely full, for example someone who stuffed himself right before the fast began.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that the יום הכפורים prohibition is defined by enjoyment and relief from affliction, not by the simple physical act of putting food in the mouth.

phrases.english: Reish Lakish said:
One who eats an overfull eating
on Yom Kippur is exempt.
What is the reason?
It is written: 'who will not be afflicted',
excluding one who harms himself.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ: הָאוֹכֵל אֲכִילָה גַּסָּה בְּיוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After defining what counts as food (Steps 14–17), the גמרא turns to a new question: what kind of eating counts.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Overfull eating on יום הכפורים is exempt, because 'affliction' excludes self-harm.

steps.title: A זר who overeats תרומה pays the קרן but not the חומש
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה quotes ריש לקיש: a זר who eats תרומה in an overfull way repays the קרן but not the חומש, because 'כי יאכל' excludes one who harms himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה said in the name of ריש לקיש: A זר (non-כהן) who ate תרומה in an overfull way pays back the value, but does not pay the extra fifth. The verse says 'if he eats', which excludes someone who is harming himself.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another teaching from ריש לקיש that uses the same idea, this time for a זר (non-כהן) who eats תרומה when he is already full.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The extra fifth (חומש) is tied to the Torah's word 'eat' (יאכל), and overfull eating is not real 'eating'. So the extra fifth is not owed. He still pays the קרן, because he destroyed food that belonged to the כהן, and that is damage no matter how it was eaten.

keyTerms.meaning: A non-כהן
The holy portion of produce given to a כהן
The principal: the basic value of what was eaten
The added fifth paid by a זר who mistakenly eats תרומה
'If he eats': the verse about a זר eating תרומה

steps.confusionAlert: He is not completely free. He still pays the קרן. Only the חומש falls away, because only the חומש depends on the act counting as 'eating'.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה אָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya said that Reish Lakish said:
A non-kohen who ate terumah in an overfull way
pays the principal
and does not pay the fifth.
'If he eats' excludes one who harms himself.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה אָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ: זָר שֶׁאָכַל תְּרוּמָה אֲכִילָה גַּסָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the same principle from Step 18 (overfull eating is self-harm, not eating) to the laws of תרומה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A זר who overeats תרומה pays the קרן but not the חומש.

steps.title: רבי ירמיה begins a related teaching in רבי יוחנן's name
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה begins quoting רבי יוחנן about a זר. The teaching continues in the next section.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה said in the name of רבי יוחנן: A זר (non-כהן)…
steps.whatsHappening: This line is a setup. רבי ירמיה starts quoting רבי יוחנן's view on the same case of a זר, and the actual ruling comes in the next section of text.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same student, רבי ירמיה, now reports a teaching from a second teacher, רבי יוחנן, about a זר who eats תרומה. This continues the same theme of eating that does not count as normal eating; the ruling itself comes on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: The אמורא who reports both teachings
Leading אמורא of ארץ ישראל, ריש לקיש's frequent partner in debate
'X said that Y said': a chain of transmission formula

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya said that Rabbi Yochanan said:
A non-kohen…
phrases.notes: The statement continues on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: זָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Introduces רבי יוחנן's teaching on the same case of a זר eating תרומה. The ruling itself appears on the next amud.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Not yet stated. The teaching continues on the next amud.
